fit: broad diet response and MDS-UPDRS daily OFF item in a Parkinson dose protocol
assessment: The diet question gives roasted potatoes or vegetables as an example within a broad category. The same protocol captures usual OFF hours in item 4.3. No potato assignment or diet-to-OFF analysis is reported.

fit: pooled fried or roasted potato in case-control food questionnaire
assessment: The intake category combines two preparations. Clinical outcomes do not give daily OFF duration by food. This questionnaire provides disease-association context without a within-Parkinson symptom comparison.

fit: encapsulated black pepper and Bunium persicum formulation and an unquantified concentration result
assessment: The primary abstract reports reduced impaired concentration in the active group. The item-level assessment and arm contrast remain unverified. The Alzheimer trial combined powdered ingredients and does not isolate cracked pepper.

fit: forehead Origanum vulgare oil exposure and depression scales
assessment: Mean depression scores declined in a 200-person paired analysis without a concurrent control. Anxiety estimates, oral dried leaves and Parkinson status were outside the reported comparison.

fit: conflicting corn versus soybean label in a postmenopausal sleep trial
assessment: The registered placebo fat is unspecified. A meeting listing says corn oil, while the original thesis and two published reports identify soybean oil. SHAPE does not supply a verified corn-oil exposure or a Parkinson insomnia comparison.
